idiom_name: stage table of function pointers + route-config flag (static-key style probe)
implementation_notes: C has no routing framework, so the Detour is hand-built: keep the destination call in one place and insert the extra stage(s) from a table of function pointers whenever the route configuration says the detour is on - the shape that gRPC/Camel users get from interceptors. The industrial-strength form of the same idea is the kernel's static keys (jump labels): a probe branch that is patched out of the instruction stream entirely while disabled, which matters when even a predicted branch is too expensive on the hot path. Keep the detour stage mutating the message in place and returning to the same delivery function, or the two legs diverge.
pitfalls: Flipping the flag from a signal handler or management thread without atomics or memory barriers: the routing thread may never observe the change, or observe it half-applied.
Letting the detour stage take ownership of a buffer the delivery path still frees (double free) or allocate a replacement the caller never releases (leak at the rejoin).
Keeping two delivery calls - one per leg - instead of one shared deliver(); the legs then drift as the code evolves.
